newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's Ershad expels top party leader.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's Ershad expels top party leader.

text.p: Bangladesh's former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad has expelled ex-prime minister Kazi Zafar Ahmed from his Jatiya Party for allegedly "overstepping party lines," Ershad's deputies said on Wednesday.
They said Ershad ordered the expulsion on Tuesday night after Ahmed was allegedly involved in a brawl with other party leaders at a Jatiya rally in Dhaka, where Ershad was the main speaker.
"Kazi Zafar Ahmed has been expelled from the party for speaking against the party's policy and ideals, and against the interest of the party chairman (Ershad)," a Jatiya Party statement said.
Jatiya sources said Ahmed had defied earlier requests by Ershad not to make "offending comments" about government policy but to stress the Jatiya Party's own independent stance.
Ershad seized power in 1982 and became president after 1984 elections. He was toppled in December 1990.
Jatiya has 33 seats in the 330 member parliament.

Ershad on Thursday rejected charges by the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party that the Jatiya Party was a crony of the government, saying it would oppose the government's actions if they were not in the interest of the people.
Ahmed was not available for comment.
